useCase.name: Mark attendance for an individual lecture rather than once for the whole day

intent.name: attendance.lecture.mark
intent.summary: Mark attendance for one period of the timetable, for the lecture assigned to the acting teacher. One step, and it says nothing about any other period.
routesHere: mark attendance for my third period maths lecture

routesHere.text: meri chauthi period ki hazri laga do
routesHere.gloss: mark attendance for my fourth period

routesHere.text: is lecture mein do bachay ghair hazir hain
routesHere.gloss: two children are absent in this lecture

routesHere.text: period ki attendance mark karo — sab present
routesHere.gloss: mark the period's attendance — everyone present

routesHere: record the register for today's second period

request.text: poore din ki hazri laga do
request.gloss: mark attendance for the whole day

routesElsewhere.note: Period marking and daily marking are separate records, and neither overwrites the other (BR-9).
A student present for three periods and absent for the rest is the pattern this use case exists to reveal (BR-8) — reading it is a separate act.

request.text: walidain ko bata do konse lecture miss hue
request.gloss: tell the parents which lectures were missed

routesElsewhere.note: Where attendance is per lecture the alert names the subjects missed (UC-05-09 BR-4).

steps.note: One step. A teacher marks only the lectures the timetable assigns to them (BR-2), and approved leave is applied before they begin (BR-4).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A lecture not assigned to the acting teacher, no lecture scheduled, a closed day, an unmarked student and a period already marked are all enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write, atomic in itself: every student's mark for that period, the stamps and the audit entry together or not at all. The mark applies to that period alone — marking a student absent in the fourth period says nothing about the fifth (BR-3). It does not touch any daily register (BR-9).

operations.name: attendance.lecture.mark
operations.idempotencyKey: lecture_id + date, since a period carries one register and a repeat returns ALREADY_MARKED
operations.purpose: Save one mark per student for a single timetabled period.

parameters.name: lecture_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No lecture matches, or none assigned to the acting user on that date.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with period, subject, class and section.

parameters.notes: A period from the timetable, scheduled to the acting teacher on that date. A lecture nobody was scheduled to teach cannot be marked (BR-2, E1, E2).

parameters.name: date
parameters.notes: Not in the future, and a working day (E3).

parameters.name: marks
parameters.notes: One entry per student on the lecture roster, each with a mark. Every student carries one (E4), and the marks come from what the actor stated.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: lecture_attendance_id
fields.description: This period's record, stored separately from every other (BR-1).

fields.name: marked_at
fields.description: The correction window runs from here (BR-5).

fields.name: counts
fields.description: present, absent, late, on_leave for this period alone (BR-3).

fields.name: pre_marked_on_leave
fields.description: Students the roster already carried as on approved leave (BR-4).

fields.name: day_pattern
fields.description: The student's marks across every period of the day, side by side — the pattern this use case exists to reveal (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The lecture is not assigned to the acting teacher.
errors.note: A teacher marks only the lectures the timetable assigns to them (BR-2).

errors.meaning: No lecture is scheduled for that period on that date.
errors.note: A period the timetable did not schedule cannot be marked (BR-11).

errors.meaning: The date is an off-day or a holiday.
A student on the roster carries no mark.
The period has already been marked.
errors.note: The message names the time. Changing it is a correction (BR-6).

planningRules.rule: Report the roster and the counts before the plan is emitted, exactly as for a daily register. "Everyone present" asserts a mark per child, and each is evidence.

Never let a mark in one period speak for another. A mark applies to that period alone (BR-3), so a request covering "the rest of the day" is several plans, one per lecture, each against a lecture the timetable assigns.
Never mark a lecture the timetable did not schedule to the acting teacher. E1 and E2 are BR-2 working — a lecture nobody was scheduled to teach has no register to write.
Never write a daily register from period marks, or the reverse. The two are separate records read side by side, and neither overwrites the other (BR-9).
Never overwrite a pre-applied leave mark. Approved leave is applied before the teacher begins so a child on sanctioned leave is not marked absent in any period (BR-4).

reversal.statement: A saved period register is not deleted or re-saved. A wrong mark is corrected through attendance.lecture.correct, and the previous mark stays visible (BR-6). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

request.text: meri chauthi period ki hazri laga do — Ayesha aur Bilal ghair hazir
request.gloss: mark my fourth period attendance — Ayesha and Bilal absent

resolvedPlans.context: Teacher, Johar Town branch. The timetable schedules them to 6-A period 4 today.

inputs.marks: $request.marks → Ayesha and Bilal Absent; the remaining 26 Present

steps.note: The roster and counts are reported first (PR-1). This says nothing about periods 3 or 5 (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Period 4's register is saved: 26 present, 2 absent. day_pattern comes back showing both students' marks across the whole day — which is what reveals a child present in the morning and gone by the afternoon (BR-8).

request.text: baaqi din ki bhi hazri laga do
request.gloss: mark the attendance for the rest of the day too

resolvedPlans.context: Teacher, Johar Town branch, assigned to periods 4 and 6.

steps.note: One plan per period, and only for periods the timetable assigns to this teacher (PR-2, PR-3).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Period 4 is marked. Report that period 6 is the actor's other lecture and needs its own marks — and that periods 1, 2, 3 and 5 belong to other teachers, so nothing here can mark them.

request.text: paanchvi period ki hazri laga do
request.gloss: mark attendance for the fifth period

resolvedPlans.context: Teacher, Johar Town branch, where period 5 is assigned to another teacher.

steps.note: Emitted unchanged. The API returns NOT_ASSIGNED (E1).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is saved. Report that period 5 is assigned to another teacher — a lecture nobody was scheduled to teach cannot be marked, and this one was scheduled to somebody else (PR-3).

intent.name: attendance.lecture.correct
intent.summary: Change a mark on a period already marked, with the reason. One step, and the previous mark stays visible.
routesHere: change Ayesha to present in period four, she was at the assembly

routesHere.text: chauthi period mein Ayesha ko present kar do
routesHere.gloss: change Ayesha to present in period four

routesHere.text: is period ka mark galat tha
bacha assembly mein tha, absent nahi tha
routesHere.gloss: the child was at the assembly, not absent

routesHere: correct the second period mark for this student

request.text: din ka mark theek kar do

routesElsewhere.note: The daily register and the period registers are separate records (BR-9).
A mark applies to that period alone (BR-3), and each correction carries its own reason.

steps.note: One step. Within the hour the teacher may change what they marked; after it the Coordinator does (BR-5, BR-7).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. A closed correction window and a missing reason are enforced by the API and arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the new mark, the previous one kept beside it, who changed it and why, together with the audit entry or not at all (BR-6). It changes that period alone — no other period and no daily register is touched (BR-3, BR-9).

operations.name: attendance.lecture.correct
operations.purpose: Change one student's mark for one period, keeping the previous mark visible.

parameters.name: lecture_attendance_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No marked period matches within the actor's scope.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the candidates with period, subject, class and when they were marked.

parameters.notes: The period's saved register, resolved from the period, class and date the actor named.

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No student on that register matches.

parameters.name: new_mark
parameters.type: enum: Present | Absent | Late | On leave
parameters.notes: What the mark becomes for this period alone (BR-3).

parameters.name: correction_reason
parameters.notes: Maximum 250 characters. Required for every change (BR-6, E6). The actor's own words.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The correction, and what it replaced.

fields.name: changed_from
fields.description: The previous mark, kept beside the new one (BR-6).

fields.name: within_teacher_window
fields.description: True where the teacher's hour had not passed (BR-5).

fields.name: day_pattern
fields.description: The student's marks across the day after the change (BR-8).

errors.meaning: The teacher's correction window has passed.
errors.note: After the hour the Coordinator makes the change (BR-7).

errors.meaning: A change was made with no reason.
The lecture is not assigned to the acting user.

planningRules.rule: Never compose the correction reason. Every change is logged with who made it and why (BR-6), and a reason nobody gave explains nothing.
Correct one period at a time. A mark applies to that period alone (BR-3), and a child absent in the fourth and present in the fifth is two facts with two reasons.
Never treat WINDOW_PASSED as something to route around. After the hour the Coordinator makes the change (BR-7).
Report the day pattern after the change. It is what the period marking exists to reveal (BR-8), and a correction that fixes one period may make the rest of the day read differently.

reversal.statement: A correction is not undone. Correcting again is another recorded change with the previous mark still visible (BR-6). The controller must not attempt a compensating call.

request.text: chauthi period mein Ayesha ko present kar do — wo assembly mein thi
request.gloss: change Ayesha to present in period four — she was at the assembly

resolvedPlans.context: Teacher, Johar Town branch, ten minutes after saving period 4.

inputs.correction_reason: Was at the school assembly during the period.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Period 4 now reads Present with Absent kept beside it. day_pattern comes back showing her whole day — report it, because the same assembly may explain period 3 too (PR-4).

request.text: teesri aur chauthi dono period theek kar do

resolvedPlans.context: Teacher, Johar Town branch, assigned to both.

steps.note: One plan per period, each with its own reason (PR-2).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Period 3 is corrected. Period 4 is a separate plan — confirm the reason applies to both before emitting the second, since a child may have been elsewhere for one and not the other.

steps.note: Emitted unchanged. The API returns WINDOW_PASSED (E5).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing changes. Report that the Coordinator makes changes after the hour, and that the teacher can ask them (PR-3).
